title: Scrapheap Survey — Informal Listing
location: General Access Terminal — The Scrapheap, Lower City Outskirts
author: Unknown — Salvager, informal notation
content:
SCRAPHEAP INVENTORY — WHAT'S ACTUALLY DOWN HERE

This is for my own use. If you're reading it you either hacked the terminal or I'm dead.

Hull count as of last walk: forty-three identifiable wrecks. Another dozen or so buried under the newer stuff.

Notable:

— A 200-ton scout variant, Imperial registry scrubbed. Aft section intact. Jump coils gone but the life support housing is usable.
— Two Fat Traders, both down. One upper deck still liveable — someone's already set up in it, I can see the power draw on the grid. Lower cargo deck flooded with chemical runoff.
— What might be a pre-Collapse hull, very deep in. Can't get close. The metal is the wrong color and the welds don't look like any technique I know. Couldn't find an access point. Left it alone.

The fake red flags at the entrance are just cloth. They're enough to keep most people out. The ones who know they're fake are already the kind of people who know to be careful anyway.

This is good real estate if you don't mind the smell and you don't mind not asking questions about what's in the lower decks of some of these hulls.

I think something is living in the pre-Collapse hull. I have not gone back to verify this.

title: Old Fat Trader — Partial Systems Log
location: General Access Terminal — The Scrapheap, Lower City Outskirts
author: Unknown — Multiple authors, Scrapheap residents
content:
This terminal has been running off a salvaged power cell for as long as anyone can remember. We use it when we have something to say.

—

'The upper deck is habitable. The lower deck is not. Don't open the cargo iris. We sealed it for a reason.'

—

'Someone has moved into the bridge. Don't know who. She has a metal arm and a very large weapon resting on the captain's chair. She has not bothered anyone. She pays the boys to run messages. I suggest we extend her the same courtesy she has extended us.' — Intelligence file on her: [[connect: ferrik_intel]]

—

'The woman in the bridge is negotiating with the gangs. I have heard her mention two of the Pirate Lords by name. She is making a case for someone who is not here. I don't know what she is offering but the boys say she pays well and doesn't ask them to go anywhere dangerous.'

—

[Most recent entry — Day 212]

'New people in the Scrapheap tonight. Not residents. Moving carefully, which means they know something. The woman in the bridge knows they are coming. I saw her adjust the machinegun when the sensors pinged.

Two separate crews came through the access tunnel tonight. Not together. Not even aware of each other. One pair came down from the upper lift and went straight toward the Fat Trader. The other pair came in from the canyon side and split, one toward the south end and the pre-Collapse hull, the other back out to the lower city.

I am going to be somewhere else for a while.'

title: Unknown Hull — Deep Scrapheap Survey Note
location: General Access Terminal — The Scrapheap, Lower City Outskirts
author: Salvager — Name: Hest Vorin (deceased, cause unrelated)
content:
I went back to look at the old hull. The one buried at the south end, under the Sindalian-era junkers.

I brought a cutter and a sensor wand.

The hull material is not in any database I have access to. Not Imperial alloy. Not Vargr standard. Not anything from the Hierate that I have ever catalogued.

The welds — or what I thought were welds — are not seams. They are part of the material itself. Like it grew that way. Like the hull was grown, not constructed.

I found what might be a hatch. No mechanism I could identify. No power draw. Just a slightly different texture in the surface, shaped like a door.

I put my hand flat against it.

The surface was warm. Not from ambient temperature — I checked. Internally warm.

I did not open it.

I am filing this note because I think someone should know it is there. I am not going back. Not for money. Not for anything.

If something lives in it, it knows I was there. I think it was polite enough not to make a thing of it.

I am choosing to interpret that as a social contract and I intend to hold up my end.

For Sindalian-era context on similar materials: [[connect: asharden_lore]]

title: Unknown Hull — Interface Attempt
location: Exterior Terminal — Unknown Hull, Deep Scrapheap, South End
author: Unknown — Automated Response
content:
There is a terminal mounted on the outer surface of the unknown hull. It was not there six years ago, according to the salvager's survey. It is there now.

The screen is already active. Nothing visible is running it. The hull surface beneath it is warm to the touch.

[INTERACTIVE TERMINAL — AWAITING INPUT]

lines: >> NOT IMPERIAL. NOT VARGR. NOT ASLAN. NOT ON FILE.
>> THE SURFACE HAS BEEN THIS TEMPERATURE FOR AT LEAST TWELVE YEARS.
>> NOTE: THIS TERMINAL HAS LOGGED YOUR BIOMETRIC SIGNATURE.
>> NOTE: WE DID NOT PROGRAM IT TO DO THAT.

steps.label: RECEIVING COORDINATE PACKET — SOURCE: INTERNAL HULL TRANSMISSION...
steps.complete_message: COORDINATE PACKET RECEIVED — NOT IN ANY KNOWN CHART

on_complete.message: The terminal displays a coordinate string that matches nothing in the Imperial charts — or any chart at all. Beneath the terminal, scratched into the hull surface in a script that predates the Third Imperium, is a single symbol. You have seen this symbol before: in the Sindalian trade manifest fragment, filed thirty years ago. In the description of the Black Glass artifact listed in the Cliff District procurement listings. Three sources. Three data points. One mark. Whatever this hull is, it is not the only one.

on_failure.message: The screen goes dark. The hull surface, which has been warm for at least twelve years according to every record anyone kept, is now cold. This is the first time this has happened. You have the distinct sense that it is deliberate.

title: Pre-Collapse Hull — Exterior Inscription Record
location: General Access Terminal — The Scrapheap, Lower City Outskirts
author: Unknown — Filed anonymously via proxy terminal

roll_check.on_success: Anonymous inscription record recovered. The symbol has appeared before.
roll_check.on_failure: File access blocked. Proxy routing stripped — no origin recoverable.

content:
Filed anonymously. The author did not want their name attached.

I spent four days photographing and transcribing the script on the hull surface. The ship at the south end. The old one.

The inscription runs the full circumference of what I believe is the vessel's equatorial line — approximately forty meters of unbroken text. It is not carved. It is not stamped. The characters appear to be part of the material itself, as though the hull was cast with them included.

I have cross-referenced the script against every database I have access to. It does not appear in any Imperial xenographic catalogue. It does not match the writing systems associated with any known spacefaring species, precursor or current.

However: one symbol appears in a Sindalian trade record fragment that was filed in the Cliff District approximately thirty years ago — describing recovered mineral items from an outer Reach site. The same symbol appears in an unrelated oral history collected at Asharden Camp. The same symbol appears scratched inside the Blood Pit arena, in a section of wall that predates the arena's current use by an estimated three hundred years.

I am not drawing a conclusion. I am noting that three separate sources, spanning at least three hundred years and three different contexts, share one mark with a hull that the salvagers cannot date and cannot open.

I am noting this and I am not going back to the hull.

For Sindalian archive context: [[connect: asharden_lore]]

title: Mercifuge Crew — Encrypted Local Broadcast
location: General Access Terminal — The Scrapheap, Lower City Outskirts
author: Signal Intercept — Source: Skull Orbital passive array

roll_check.on_success: Compressed signal decoded. The Mercifuge crew has been checking in. Something has changed.
roll_check.on_failure: Signal too compressed to decode at this access level. Encryption layer intact.

content:
PASSIVE INTERCEPT — SKULL ORBITAL — SIGNAL LOG

Source: Bay 7-C vessel, Mercifuge. Timing: every four hours since arrival, three days running.
Format: Compressed burst, tight-beam, aimed at the lower city.
Recipient: No registration. The address resolves to a relay node in the canyon level.

Decrypt of most recent burst (partial — encryption partial):

'...still no movement on the hull. She says she's close but the second contact complicates things. Two crews now, not one. She needs another day at minimum. She says the other crew may be useful or may be a problem. She does not know yet.'

'...the item in Bay 7-C storage has been registering temperature fluctuation. Not from ambient. We have sealed the cargo bay as a precaution. Suggest she conclude negotiations and return before we have to make a decision about it ourselves.'

— End of partial decrypt —

Note: The 'item in Bay 7-C storage' is not listed on the Mercifuge manifest. Bay 7-C is Skull Orbital's designation. The item appears to have been loaded before the ship docked.

Note: The cargo bay temperature fluctuation is not a mechanical fault. Three inspections have confirmed the ship's systems are nominal. The fluctuation is internal to the sealed cargo only.

title: Heat Signature Survey — Southern Sector Grid
location: Survey Terminal — Scrapheap, Central Gantry Access Panel
author: Scrapheap Environmental Monitoring Array — Automated
content:
The scrapheap environmental grid runs passive thermal monitoring to flag hull fires before they spread. The southern sector has been flagging an anomaly for at least twelve years. The survey terminal at the central gantry allows active scanning of the grid.

[INTERACTIVE TERMINAL — AWAITING INPUT]

lines: >> SCRAPHEAP ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING — THERMAL GRID v1.4
>> ANOMALY DURATION: APPROX. 4,380 DAYS (12 YEARS, ESTIMATED)

options: NORTH SECTOR — Entry access, Fat Trader wrecks
CENTRAL SECTOR — Main gantry, active salvage area
EAST SECTOR — Chemical runoff zone, lower pens
SOUTH SECTOR — Deep scrapheap, buried hulls

steps.label: PROCESSING THERMAL GRID DATA — SOUTHERN SECTOR...

lines: >> ANOMALOUS HULL — SOUTHERN END, BENEATH SINDALIAN-ERA JUNKERS:
>> INTERNAL TEMPERATURE: COULD NOT RESOLVE — SENSOR RETURNS INCONSISTENT
>> THIS READING HAS NOT CHANGED IN 12 YEARS.
>> NOTE: SCAN PING ACKNOWLEDGED BY SOURCE.
>> NOTE: SURFACE TEMPERATURE INCREASED BY 0.3°C DURING ACTIVE SCAN.
>> NOTE: THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THE ANOMALY HAS RESPONDED TO INPUT.

on_complete.message: The thermal scan found what twelve years of passive monitoring had already logged: a hull in the south end of the Scrapheap running 13 degrees above ambient with no power source and no explanation. What the passive system never logged before is that the hull responded to the active scan. The surface temperature rose by a third of a degree the moment the scan ping hit it. It noticed you looking. For more on the hull itself and the terminal mounted on its surface: [[connect: scrapheap]]

on_failure.message: SCAN ABORTED. Grid sensor array returned a null read on the southern sector — every sensor in that zone simultaneously returned zero, then came back online showing ambient temperature only. The anomalous reading is gone. The hull that has been running warm for twelve years is, according to the grid, now at exactly 18.2°C. The grid has never returned a null read in that sector before.
